To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the work climate, student motivation, and teachers basic psychological needs can predict clinical teachers' motivation to teacher and that clinical teachers motivation can predict teaching approaches.

clinical teachers' perceptions of a work climate characterized as supportive and students' autonomous motivations predict the satisfaction of clinical teachers' basic psychological need, which in turn predict clinical teachers' motivation to teaching, which predicts student centered teaching approaches.

teachers' perceptions of a supportive work climate, students autonomous motivation, and satisfaction of their basic needs predict autonomous motivation to teach, which in turn is related to student centered teaching approaches.
In summary, our research is concerned with
promoting a positive learning environment that is characterized by a positive work climate, students with high levels of motivation, and teachers with high levels of autonomy.
promoting an optimal learning environment for students and clinical teachers.
the importance of understanding the motivational processes of clinical teachers in order to promote optimal learning environments for students.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
teachers who perceive a supportive work climate and their students' autonomous motivation are satisfied with their basic psychological needs which leads to autonomous motivation to teaching.

the satisfaction of clinical teachers' basic psychological need for autonomy, competence, and relatedness, is associated with their autonomous motivation to teach and that this autonomous motivation to teach, is associated with a more student centered teaching approach.

the results of this study suggest that clinical teachers are more likely to be motivated to teach when they perceive that their students are motivated and when they perceive a work climate characterized as supportive.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the work climate, student's motivation, and teachers basic psychological needs satisfaction predict teachers' motivation to teaching.
teachers' motivation to work with their students can be enhanced when the work climate is characterized by a supportive teacher-supervisor relationship and when students are motivated to learn.
the work climate, student motivation, teachers' basic psychological need satisfaction and motivation to teach are associated with student centered teaching approaches.
The main takeaway from our work is that
clinical teachers' motivation to work with their students can be predicted by the work climate they experience in the clinic.

clinical teachers' perceptions of their students' motivation, their work climate, and their basic psychological needs satisfaction are important factors to consider in order to foster their optimal motivation and, consequently, their student centered teaching approaches.

clinical teachers' motivation to engage in student centered teaching practices is positively associated with students' autonomous motivation and negatively associated with their controlled motivation. (C) 2019 Elsevier Ltd and ANZCA & FPM. All
